title: Diver Medical Participant Questionnaire
description: Standard recreational diving medical screening questionnaire designed to identify potential hyperbaric medical contraindications.

primary_questions.text: I have had problems with my lungs/breathing, heart, or blood affecting my normal physical or mental performance.
I am over 45 years of age and can answer YES to any of the following: I smoke, have high cholesterol, high blood pressure, or a family history of heart disease.
I struggle to perform moderate exercise (for example, walking 1.6 kilometers / one mile in 14 minutes or swimming 200 meters / yards without resting).
I have had problems with my eyes, ears, or nasal passages/sinuses.
I have had surgery within the last 12 months, or have ongoing problems related to past surgery.
I have lost consciousness, had migraine headaches, seizures, stroke, significant head injury, or suffer from persistent neurological injury or disease.

I am currently undergoing treatment (or have required treatment within the last five years) for psychological problems, personality disorder, panic attacks, or an addiction to drugs or alcohol; or, I have been diagnosed with a learning or developmental disability.
I have had back problems, hernia, ulcers, or diabetes.
I have had stomach or intestine problems, including recent diarrhea.
I am taking prescription medications (with the exception of birth control or anti-malarial drugs other than mefloquine/Lariam).

questions.text: Chest surgery, heart surgery, heart attack, or heart disease.
Persistent chest pain or discomfort with exertion.
Asthma, wheezing, severe allergies, or reactive airway disease within the last 12 months.
Recurrent bronchitis, persistent cough, or emphysema.
Collapsed lung (pneumothorax) or chest trauma.
High blood pressure or taking blood pressure medication.
Elevated cholesterol or taking cholesterol medication.
Current cigarette, cigar, or pipe smoker.
Back surgery or persistent back/joint problems affecting movement.
Hernia repair or uncorrected hernia.
Type 1 or Type 2 Diabetes.
Epilepsy, seizures, convulsions, or taking anti-seizure medication.
Recurrent fainting episodes, blackouts, or transient ischemic attack (TIA).
Severe migraines or cluster headaches within the last 12 months.
Depression, anxiety, panic disorder, or bipolar disorder requiring medication.
ADHD, autism spectrum, or learning differences affecting safety instructions.
Difficulty equalizing ears in airplanes or underwater.
Frequent sinus infections or sinus surgery.
Perforated eardrum or ear surgery.
Bleeding or blood disorder (e.g. hemophilia, anemia, taking blood thinners).
Active stomach or duodenal ulcer.
